newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel stands by nuclear fuel programme.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel stands by nuclear fuel programme.

text.p: A government panel said on Friday Japan should press ahead with its nuclear fuel recycling programme despite recurring accidents at nuclear power facilities.
The panel report coincided with but was unrelated to a decision by France on Thursday to abandon its fast-breeder nuclear reactor programme.
Japan's nuclear fuel recycling programme aims to recycle spent fuel produced at commercial reactors by separating the used fuel into nuclear waste and reusable uranium and plutonium.
A fast-breeder nuclear reactor, which produces more plutonium than it uses, is a vital part of the programme.

"The importance of the nuclear fuel cycle programme has not changed at all (after a series of accidents at fast-breeder reactor Monju and at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant)," Riichiro Chikaoka, head of the Atomic Energy Commission, said in a statement.
Chikaoka is also the director general of the Science and Technology Agency.
The statement made clear the commission, the ultimate decision maker of Japan's nuclear power policy, has not changed its stance even after the recent string of accidents.
Panel members approved the statement on Friday in spite of the French government decision to axe its fast-breeder reactor, an agency official said.
France's Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday he would scrap the fault-prone Superphenix fast-breeder reactor, describing it as too costly and of doubtful value.
